title: Late shift ops scratchpad - 02:00 handoff draft
body:
TL;DR:
- Quiet night overall; intermittent 503 spike (~0.7%) observed in hosted API between 01:10–01:35 UTC; spike correlated with short KV-cache GC on 3 inference pods (eu-west-1).
- Temporary mitigation applied: routed affected traffic to fallback model variant (gpt-13b-fp16) and increased average batch size limit to reduce burst pressure.
- Action items for incoming shift: keep an eye on latency tail and check whether the rollout (deploy/2026-02-26/quant-v2) shows further regressions; follow rollback steps below if 503 > 1% for 10m.

Context / timeline (notes):
- 00:45 UTC: Scheduled small config push (quantization profile v2) to canary (canary-pool-1).
- 01:05 UTC: Alert: 503-rate > 0.5% for 5m on hosted-api-prod route /v1/generate.
- 01:12 UTC: Observed repeated KV-cache GC logs (eviction spikes) on pods inference-eu-02/03/07.
- 01:18 UTC: Manual routing change -> fallback to gpt-13b-fp16; 503 rate dropped to baseline in ~3m.
- 01:40 UTC: Increased batching cap for eu region from 6 -> 8 to smooth bursts; monitoring.

Current state:
- Incidents: none open (I suppressed the noise alert after mitigation), but monitoring set for 503-rate threshold.
- Recent deploys: quant-v2 (2026-02-26) rolled to 70% at 23:40 UTC, canary to 100% for some pools.
- Customer impact: small fraction of requests saw failed responses during 01:05–01:18; no escalations from support yet.

Known flakey surfaces / debug pointers (why this kept happening):
- Quantization v2 temporarily increases memory per-inference step which reduces effective cache headroom; when multiple requests with long context align it pushes the runtime to prune K/V cache causing short tail latencies and 503s.
- Autoscaler loop for dedicated pools (scale-to-zero guard) can cause tight pod churn when combined with bursty traffic and aggressive prefix cache eviction.

Immediate steps (if you see 503-rate > 1% sustained for 10m):
1) Confirm alerts in Datadog and correlate with pod logs: filter for "kv_cache_eviction" and GC timestamps.
2) If eviction is repeated on >2 pods, run rollback to previous quant profile for affected pools (commands below).
3) If rollback not possible quickly, set routing policy to fallback model variant for the region and raise batch cap.
4) Create a postmortem stub (JIRA OPS ticket) and assign to "applied-ml" and "serving-runtime" owners.

Runbook draft (quick steps) — copy into official runbook after verifying: 
- Check alerts:
  - Datadog: monitor.metric(ingress.503_rate.by_region) > 0.01  // 1% threshold
  - Logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference -c runner --since=15m | grep -E "kv_cache_eviction|OOM|traceback"
- Rollback quant profile (safe rollback):
  - rictl model set-variant --model redwood/gpt-13b --variant quant-v1 --pools eu-west-1
  - rictl rollout status --model redwood/gpt-13b --variant quant-v1 --timeout 10m
- Temporary routing fallback (if rollback takes long):
  - rictl routing set --route /v1/generate --policy region-prefer --fallback redwood/gpt-13b-fp16 --region eu-west-1
  - rictl routing get --route /v1/generate --region eu-west-1  # verify
- Cache warm/force refresh (experimental):
  - rictl cache flush --model redwood/gpt-13b --pools eu-west-1 --grace 30s  # use cautiously
- Scale guard (if autoscaler misbehaving):
  - kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3}}'  # prevent scale-to-zero churn during incident

Notes to next shift:
- Keep the quant-v2 rollout frozen until AM sync with Applied ML and Serving Runtime teams.
- If you need to escalate, page Platform Lead (@ravi_kumar) then Applied-ML (@elena_park). Include request id examples and exact pod IDs.

Open follow-ups (my TODOs I didn't finish):
- Add explicit metric for kv_cache_eviction_count to Datadog (ticket created, waiting on metrics infra team).
- Capture a sample trace mapping request -> kv_gc timeline (need tracing flags enabled on runner).
- Draft a short customer note template in support doc in case we need to communicate recurrence.

Random scratch notes / one-liners (for transfer):
- If you see "oom_alloc: failed" in runner logs, that's probably quant memory bump, fallback immediately.
- Watch for >20% CPU on pod inference-eu-07 — that one historically flips hard under burst.
- Slack snippets to use: "We're routing to fallback model variant while we investigate a short-lived performance regression. No customer data exposure."
checklist: Verify Datadog 503-rate and latency p99 for /v1/generate
Check pod logs for kv_cache_eviction and OOM traces
Confirm routing policy for eu-west-1 (rictl routing get)
If needed, rollback quant profile to quant-v1
Update JIRA stub and tag applied-ml + serving-runtime
